_notes.purpose: Development-only seed data for the Rideau Community Hub prototype.
_notes.editing: Flat arrays mirroring the Prisma models in prisma/schema.prisma. Cross-references use the explicit `id` fields below (users.organizationId -> organizations.id, events.ownerId -> users.id). Ids are only meaningful inside this file; the seed script is responsible for mapping them onto real autoincrement primary keys.
_notes.passwords: `devPassword` is plaintext and exists only so the seed script can hash it with argon2 before writing to users.password_hash. Each user is hashed separately, so users sharing a password still get distinct hashes (argon2 salts per call). Never ship this file to a non-development environment.
_notes.datetimes: ISO 8601 with an explicit UTC offset. Ottawa is -04:00 (EDT) until DST ends on 1 November 2026 and -05:00 (EST) after it, so both appear below. Events are dated relative to 2026-08-03: a couple in the past, the rest running about four months forward. GET /v1/events defaults startDate to now, so past events are excluded unless a window explicitly asks for them - which is why a few are kept here.
_notes.organizationTags: Must be one of: Advocacy, Civic, Community, Culture, Education, Equity, Indigenous, Makers, Policy, Research, Seniors, Settlement, Tech, Volunteer, Youth. Enforced by a CHECK in the initial migration.
_notes.images: organizations.logo uses a shared placeholder path; no logo assets exist in the repo yet. events.thumbnail is left null for the same reason.
_notes.eventTags: The frontend's `Registration` / `Volunteers wanted` chips have no column in the schema, so they are represented by the presence of registrationLink / volunteerContact respectively.
_notes.events: Every event runs 1-3 hours, and endsAt must be strictly after startsAt - the events table CHECKs it. The cluster sharing one day exists to exercise a full calendar cell.
_notes.organizations: These are real Ottawa-area organizations. Do not invent new ones to fill out the data - names, contacts and websites here stand in for real entities and the .example domains keep them inert.

organizations.name: Rideau-Rockcliffe Community Resource Centre
organizations.blurb: A neighbourhood anchor offering settlement, employment, family, and seniors programming across Ottawa's east end.

organizations.name: Council on Aging of Ottawa
organizations.blurb: Advocacy and convening for older adults, championing age-friendly policy and connection across the city.

organizations.name: Odawa Native Friendship Centre
organizations.blurb: A welcoming gathering place delivering culturally grounded programs and supports for the urban Indigenous community.

organizations.name: Social Planning Council of Ottawa
organizations.blurb: Research, policy, and community development working toward a more equitable and inclusive Ottawa.

organizations.name: STEAMakers Guild
organizations.blurb: Hands-on science, tech, engineering, art, and math workshops for curious makers of every age.

organizations.name: Ottawa Civic Tech
organizations.blurb: Volunteers building open, public-interest technology with and for the Ottawa community.

events.title: Newcomer Welcome Morning
events.description: A relaxed drop-in for newcomers to the neighbourhood. Meet settlement workers, learn what programs are running this summer, and connect with other families over coffee.

events.title: Commons Fabric Meetup (July)
events.description: Monthly working session for the Commons Fabric project. Newcomers welcome — we'll walk through the calendar prototype and pick up open tasks together.

events.title: Summer Lunch Drop-in
events.description: A free community lunch, every Monday through the summer. No sign-up, no cost — just come and share a table with your neighbours.

events.title: Evening Craft Circle
events.description: Wind down the day with a laid-back making session — bring a project or start something new. Materials provided while they last.

events.title: Tech Help Desk for Seniors
events.description: Bring your phone, tablet or laptop and a question. Volunteers sit with you one-to-one for as long as it takes — no question too small.

events.title: Housing Data Working Group
events.description: Monthly working session on the neighbourhood housing dashboard. We review new data, agree what it says, and decide what to publish.

events.title: Beading Circle
events.description: An open beading circle for all skill levels. Bring your own work or learn a starter pattern with us. Tea and bannock provided.

events.title: Fall Program Registration Opens
events.description: In-person registration for autumn programming — language classes, employment workshops, after-school care and seniors' fitness. Staff on hand to help you choose.

events.title: Age-Friendly Ottawa Town Hall
events.description: An open conversation about making Ottawa more age-friendly. Bring your ideas on transit, housing, and connection — your input shapes this year's advocacy priorities.

events.title: Family Maker Lab: Circuits
events.description: Hands-on electronics for curious makers aged 8 and up. Build a working circuit you can take home — no experience needed, just bring your curiosity.

events.title: Open Data Night
events.description: Bring a dataset or a question. We poke at open civic data together and see what the city is quietly telling us.

events.title: Powwow Planning Circle
events.description: Open planning session for the autumn powwow. Dancers, drummers, vendors and volunteers all welcome — come hear the plan and find your place in it.

events.title: Commons Fabric Meetup
events.description: Monthly working session for the Commons Fabric project. Newcomers welcome — we'll walk through the calendar prototype and pick up open tasks together.

events.title: Employment Skills Workshop
events.description: A practical afternoon on résumés, Canadian workplace norms and interview practice, with one-to-one review at the end.

events.title: Autumn Powwow (Day 1)
events.description: Day one of our autumn powwow — a celebration of culture, dance, and community. Grand entry at noon, followed by drumming, dancing, craft and food vendors. All are welcome.

events.title: Autumn Powwow (Day 2)
events.description: Day two of our autumn powwow. Grand entry at noon, special performances, honour songs, and a community feast to close the weekend.

events.title: Poverty & Policy Briefing
events.description: A lunchtime briefing on the latest local data around income, housing, and food security, with time for discussion on where research can drive change.

events.title: Falls Prevention Clinic
events.description: A practical session on balance, strength and making your home safer, run with a physiotherapist. Free, and repeated each season.

events.title: Repair Cafe
events.description: Bring something broken — a lamp, a toaster, a wobbly chair — and fix it alongside a volunteer who knows how. Free, and the parts bin is open.

events.title: Community Potluck Brunch
events.description: Bring a dish to share and meet your neighbours over a relaxed brunch. Vegetarian and halal options always welcome.

events.title: Civic Tech Show & Tell
events.description: Five-minute demos of things people have built for the city, followed by questions and the usual arguing about maps.

events.title: Winter Readiness for Seniors
events.description: What to line up before the snow arrives: snow-clearing help, transport options, grocery delivery and check-in calls.

events.title: Winter Solstice Feast
events.description: A shared meal to mark the turning of the year, with storytelling and a round dance to follow. All are welcome; bring a dish if you can.

events.title: Holiday Hamper Packing
events.description: Volunteers pack and sort hampers for delivery across the neighbourhood. Two-hour shifts, all ages welcome with an adult.
